subject.title: feat: sign stored OpenClaw catalog publications

question: Should this route switch require an atomic, rotation-versioned signer contract before merge, while retaining the proposed fail-closed behavior for missing or invalid signing configuration?
rationale: This choice defines the production key-rotation trust boundary and whether an upgrade may intentionally make the existing public feed unavailable until operator secrets and the OpenClaw trust root are coordinated.

options.title: Require Atomic Rotation Before Merge
options.body: Store or activate the key id and private key atomically, bind validators to the signed-representation revision, add rotation tests, and keep fail-closed behavior only with coordinated deployment proof.

options.title: Defer The Public Route Switch
options.body: Land or retain preparatory signing code without replacing the existing unsigned public route until the RFC, consumer trust root, production key, and rollout procedure are ready together.

options.title: Accept A Maintenance Window
options.body: Intentionally permit temporary 503 responses during a documented disable-first rotation, but still prevent any mixed-pair 200 response and stale-validator result.

recommendation.title: Require Atomic Rotation Before Merge
recommendation.body: Store or activate the key id and private key atomically, bind validators to the signed-representation revision, add rotation tests, and keep fail-closed behavior only with coordinated deployment proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They performed the current-head cross-contract review and identified the exact rotation and validator requirements that need a security-boundary decision.
